artifacts.summary: Generator behaviour, machine-checked scratch-copy simulation (KTypeSummary preserved 6/6; RaySummary 13/16 with three descriptions truncated at escaped pipes; one-line escape-aware split preserves 16/16), recurrence evidence, three-tier sweep of ~33 unwrapped Lines-bearing tables (~29 stale), task 731 auto-coverage, and the INV-red territory hazard on sibling 812's three rollup files.

user_decision.question: Three RaySummary description cells contain GFM-escaped pipes (\|) that the generator's split_row truncates on regeneration; how should the task resolve this before wrapping?
options: Option A — rewrite the inline Lean notation in RaySummary README rows 41/43/45 so no pipe remains, keeping the generator untouched per the record's NON-GOALS

Option B — make split_row escape-aware with the verified one-line re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", body) change in scripts/check-module-invariants.sh (preserves all 16 descriptions byte-for-byte; a stated one-line deviation from the NON-GOAL)
Option C — register RaySummary as hand-maintained and wrap only KTypeSummary (does not meet the task's goal for RaySummary)
user_decision.recommended: Option B — make split_row escape-aware with the verified one-line re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", body) change in scripts/check-module-invariants.sh (preserves all 16 descriptions byte-for-byte; a stated one-line deviation from the NON-GOAL)

claim_invalidations.claim: The claim that check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory preserves every hand-written trailing description byte-for-byte is false for any row whose description contains an escaped pipe: three RaySummary rows (HitComplete, AnchorLayer, LadderModel) are truncated to their last fragment, shown by a verbatim scratch-copy run of the generator.

memory_candidates.content: check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory parses existing table rows with a plain body.split('|'), so a description cell containing a GFM-escaped pipe (\|) is truncated to the text after its last pipe on regeneration, and INV is green afterwards. Before wrapping any README table in BEGIN GENERATED markers, grep the rows for '\|'; a one-line re.split(r'(?<!\\)\|', body) in split_row makes it escape-aware (verified byte-for-byte on 16 rows). Also: rows whose file no longer exists are dropped silently with their description unless the path resolves relative to dir= (pinned rows like ../X.lean survive).

To dry-run check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory on specific files without touching the tree: extract the Python heredoc verbatim (awk between python3 - <<'PYEOF' and PYEOF), replace only the line 'for target in markdown_targets():' with an env-var path list, and run it from the repo root so dir= resolves against the live tree. Running --check, then write, then --check on scratch copies gives FAIL/rewrote/PASS plus a diffable before/after; a key-wise description comparison then proves preservation. This also avoids the whole-tree writer rewriting stale blocks in a concurrent sibling's file territory.

The INV check in check-module-invariants.sh covers only wrapped BEGIN GENERATED blocks and INVENTORY: hand-maintained registrations (existence audit only, not counts). As of 2026-10-17 about 33 README inventory tables under FormalSystem/ carry a Lines column with no marker and ~29 of them are stale; hand reconciles have been observed to write already-wrong counts. Whole-tree rollup blocks (README.md, FormalSystem/README.md, FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md) go INV-red whenever any .lean file is added anywhere, so during a multi-task cycle the INV exit code may be red for reasons outside a given task; key on the FAIL output's named-file list instead.
